# Pull Request Template

## Description
Provide a clear and concise description of the purpose of this pull request. Include context, motivation, and what issue or feature it addresses.

Fixes: # (issue ID)

---

## Type of Change
Select the type that best describes this pull request:

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor or code cleanup
- [ ] Infrastructure or CI/CD update

---

## Implementation Details
Briefly describe what was changed in the codebase:

- What modules, files, or functions were added/modified.
- Relevant dependencies or configuration changes.
- Any breaking changes that other developers should be aware of.

---

## Testing
Explain how you tested your changes:

- [ ] All existing tests pass.
- [ ] New tests added and verified.
- [ ] Manual verification performed.

Include details such as:
- Test environment (OS, Node/Elixir version, etc.).
- Steps to reproduce or verify the result.

---

## Checklist
Before submitting, ensure all of the following are complete:

- [ ] Code builds and runs locally without errors.
- [ ] Linting and formatting checks pass.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable).
- [ ] Linked issue or Jira ticket referenced in the PR title.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria satisfied (see project guidelines).

---

## Screenshots / Visuals (if applicable)
Attach screenshots, logs, or other outputs that illustrate the change.

---

## Additional Notes
Add any context, technical debt, or follow-up work related to this PR.

---
